source.title: Rethinking Normalization Placement for LLMs: Post-Norm under Curriculum Depth Growing
source.authors: Sheng Ren; Ya-Dong Wang; Nai-Qiang Tan; Jian-Gang Kong; Jun Fang; Rui Liu; Jun Wang; Kai Chen; Li Liang; Xiang Chen

record.tranche_reason: Tests normalization placement and depth-growth training in a block-stack LLM distillation setting, an extension beyond the claim versions’ stated CIFAR, toy-network, and batch-normalization settings.
record.gate_note: Reports validation cross-entropy, phase-wise validation loss, and diagnostic measurements for its own trained students. These do not measure training classification error or show whether the claim’s benchmark recipes reach zero training error. Cited results from prior work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests RMSNorm placement and staged depth growth in Transformer distillation, which none of V1–V6 names. It does not compare initialization schemes, plain versus residual networks, batch normalization versus no normalization, or learning rates relative to stability thresholds. Its validation losses and boundary diagnostics therefore do not test these versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that normalization placement and depth curriculum interact in this distillation setting: joint training nearly ties, while growth favors post-norm. They associate this with boundary-scale conditioning, while acknowledging that the diagnostics do not establish causation and the freeze control cannot exclude backward-at-append effects.
record.recipe_differences: LLM block-stack distillation using AdamW and staged depth growth; evaluates validation CE and boundary diagnostics rather than CIFAR training classification error. The teacher embedding is frozen, and the LM head is teacher-initialized and trainable.
record.method_sensitivity: Normalization placement ranking differs between joint and grow protocols; phase-wise ranking crosses after blocks are appended. Results concern a single reported seed (42).

fits_no_version.finding: Joint-training validation CE is nearly equal for pre-norm and post-norm (2.7603 versus 2.7607), while post-norm performs better under growth (2.7330 versus 2.7658). Extended post-joint controls remain worse at 2.7518 and 2.7428. The placement gap persists when earlier blocks are frozen.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: RMSNorm placement interacts with the depth-growth training protocol in the tested Transformer distillation setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Pre-norm growth exhibits structural-token boundary-scale drift and a nearly identity-mapped final block; post-norm controls boundary scales and shows substantial whole-block removal sensitivity. These diagnostics are observational.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Boundary-scale conditioning is a candidate explanation for the post-norm growth advantage, without establishing it as the sole cause.

record.problems: Primary runs use seed 42 only. Main outcomes are held-out validation CE/PPL rather than training classification error. Boundary-scale diagnostics are observational, and the authors state freeze does not isolate forward conditioning from backward-at-append effects.
record.rows_left_out: None of the reported result rows were omitted.

untested.parts: All parts: CIFAR training classification error, random or corrupted labels, and size, stopping or regularization effects.
All parts: two-layer ReLU spurious minima and extra student neurons relative to teacher width.
All parts: training degradation in plain convolutional networks, its prevention by identity shortcuts, and the special-initialization and Fixup cases.
All parts: activation-matched initialization comparisons, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, training speed and achievable plain-network depth.
All parts: stability thresholds, curvature or sharpness dynamics, catapult recovery and divergence. Append-induced loss jumps and scheduled learning-rate restarts do not test these.
All parts: batch normalization versus no normalization, accuracy gain speed, higher-learning-rate tolerance and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: Replace the reader's tests/T3 classification with discusses/T6. Fixup is cited as background, without testing or operationally relying on its reported finding. Results use one reported seed. No omitted result bears on V1–V6.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/100 training classification error, random or corrupted labels, and model size or training duration effects.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local minima and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus shortcut networks, depth-related training classification error, and the stated special-initialization and normalization-free cases.
Comparisons of initialization schemes, signal or gradient propagation, and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to stability limits, loss recovery or divergence, and sharpness.
Batch normalization comparisons, accuracy gain speed, and learning-rate tolerance.
